Some of these rumors appear so frequently, and in such complex, colorful, and entertaining ways that we can think of them as academic urban legends. The explanation for this phenomenon is usually that authors have lazily, sloppily, or fraudulently employed sources, and peer reviewers and editors have not discovered these weaknesses in the manuscripts during evaluation. To illustrate this phenomenon, I draw upon a remarkable case in which a decimal point error appears to have misled millions into believing that spinach is a good nutritional source of iron. Through this example, I demonstrate how an academic urban legend can be conceived and born, and can continue to grow and reproduce within academia and beyond.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1177\/0306312714535679","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2014,6,13]],"date-time":"2014-06-13T03:43:02Z","timestamp":1402630982000},"page":"638-654","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1177\/sage-journals-update-policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":62,"title":["Academic urban legends"],"prefix":"10.1177","volume":"44","author":[{"given":"Ole Bj\u00f8rn","family":"Rekdal","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Faculty of Health and Social Sciences, Bergen University College, Bergen, Norway"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"179","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2014,6,12]]},"reference":[{"key":"bibr1-0306312714535679","volume-title":"Baby Facts: The Truth about Your Child\u2019s Health, from Newborn through Preschool","author":"Adesman A","year":"2009"},{"key":"bibr2-0306312714535679","volume-title":"AMA Manual of Style: A Guide for Authors and Editors","author":"American Medical Association","year":"2007","edition":"10"},{"key":"bibr3-0306312714535679","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.1177\/030631293023001003"},{"key":"bibr4-0306312714535679","unstructured":"Bauerlein M, Gad-el-Hak M, Grody W, McKelvey B, Trimble SW (2010) We must stop the avalanche of low-quality research.
